knowledge_gaps: The gate controls an added recent-history branch, but does not explicitly separate persistent preferences from recent intent: SASRec already includes recent interactions. Compare against simple recent-item pooling and fixed residual mixtures before attributing gains to learned timescale selection.

The architecture is underspecified: gate dimensionality, projection, initialization, dropout, pooling denominator, and truncated-prefix length need definitions. LayerNorm(h + g * project(r)) does not necessarily recover baseline SASRec when g approaches zero.

Negative sampling needs explicit replacement and duplicate rules, bounded handling of small eligible catalogs, and per-position causal masking. Prefix-positive exclusion also prevents previously observed items from serving as negatives, which may affect repeated-item behavior.

The four-way ablation lacks a GPU-time allocation, checkpoint-selection schedule, and fixed tuning ranges. Repeated selection on 200 validation users per category risks validation overfitting; paired uncertainty estimates would help assess small gains.

Raw margins depend on embedding norms and objective scale, so BCE and softmax margins are not directly comparable. The originality score is reasonable, but potential and implementation difficulty remain provisional without runtime measurements or evidence that fusion adds value beyond the loss change.
